title: Edge Deployment Data Handling and Ops SLA (Template)
content:
Purpose: This is a template (working draft) for customer-facing Service Level and Data Handling terms that apply when Redwood Inference software (the "Service") is deployed to customer-managed edge environments (including customer data centers, branch sites, or third-party co-location where Redwood maintains an operational footprint). This exhibit is intended to be attached to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) as an "Edge Deployment Data Handling and Ops SLA".

Scope and Applicability:
- Applies only to components explicitly listed in Schedule A (Edge Components) and any additional components mutually agreed in writing.
- Does NOT override general provisions of the MSA except where this exhibit explicitly states otherwise.

Definitions (selected):
- "Edge Environment": customer-managed network, physical or virtual infrastructure where Service components are installed.
- "Edge Data": any Customer Data that is collected, processed, cached, or stored by Service components located in the Edge Environment.
- "On-device Cache": transient model state, token caches, or K/V caches persisted on local storage for performance reasons.
- "Operational Evidence": logs, traces, and artifacts provided to Customer or third-party auditor per the Audit and Evidence section.

Data Classification and Handling Rules:
1) Classification: Customer will supply classification labels for any dataset or stream designated for Edge processing (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated). Redwood will enforce handling rules mapped to these labels.
2) Minimization: Edge components must be configured to minimize persisted data by default. Default retention for On-device Cache is 24 hours unless otherwise approved.
3) Encryption: At-rest and in-transit encryption is mandatory for all Edge Data. Acceptable algorithms and key lengths are specified in Appendix 1 (e.g., AES-256-GCM for at-rest; TLS 1.3 for in-transit).
4) Key Custody: Customer holds primary KMS control for private-key material where requested. Redwood offers KMIP/Cloud-KMS integrations; if Customer-supplied KMS is used, Redwood will not retain plaintext keys.
5) Ephemeral Secrets: Session-level secrets used for request signing are rotated automatically every 12 hours by default.

Operational SLA (availability & maintenance windows):
- Availability target for Edge Controller component: 99.5% monthly uptime measured at the controller API endpoint, excluding scheduled maintenance and Customer-caused outages.
- Incident classification and response times (initial acknowledgement):
  * Sev 1 (service down or data exfiltration suspected): 30 minutes
  * Sev 2 (degraded performance that impacts production latency SLOs): 2 hours
  * Sev 3 (minor impact, operational question): 24 hours
- Maintenance windows: Redwood will propose maintenance windows at least 7 days in advance for non-emergency changes. Emergency patches (security hotfixes) will be communicated as soon as possible and executed per the Emergency Patch Procedure.

Patch, Upgrade and Rollback Controls:
- Planned upgrades require a minimum 14-day notice for scheduled rollouts; can include canary cohorts and automatic rollback policies.
- Rollback capability: All orchestrated changes must be able to roll back to the last stable revision within the same maintenance window unless explicitly waived.
- Binary provenance and integrity: All deployed artifacts must be signed; Customer may request SBOM and signature verification evidence.

Logging, Telemetry and Evidence Exchange:
- Minimum telemetry set: error logs, request traces (sampled), resource utilization metrics, and security audit events.
- Sensitive fields in logs (PII, tokens) must be redacted at source before leaving the Edge Environment unless Customer explicitly authorizes retention for troubleshooting.
- Evidence delivery: per-request logs and traces will be made available via secure channels for 90 days. Longer retention can be negotiated as an add-on.

Data Access, Deletion and Return:
- Data deletion request: Redwood will provide a documented procedure and automation hooks for bulk deletion of Edge Data. Standard deletion SLA: 10 business days to provide deletion artifacts and confirmation.
- At termination: Redwood will purge its service-side snapshots of Edge Data within 30 days and assist Customer in remote wipe of any caches when feasible.

Audit Rights and Third-Party Assessments:
- Customer may request an annual audit with 30 days' notice. Audit scope and evidence requests must be mutually agreed.
- For high-risk customers, a joint on-site review of procedures may be scheduled; Redwood may propose a redaction/NDAs for sensitive operational details.

Security Controls and Hardening:
- Default hardening: all edge hosts should run with least-privilege service accounts, disk encryption enabled, and kernel-level mitigations per Appendix 2.
- Network segmentation: control plane traffic must be isolated from application data plane via VLANs or firewall rules; explicit port lists and IP ranges must be approved prior to deployment.
- Runtime integrity monitoring: optional module for tamper detection can be enabled and configured to send alerts to the Customer SOC.

Incident Response and Notification:
- Notification windows: Redwood will notify Customer within 1 hour of detection of a confirmed security incident affecting Edge Components; full incident report delivered within 7 business days (interim reports as available).
- Containment: Redwood will coordinate containment actions with Customer and may, with written approval, apply temporary mitigations (e.g., block network egress) to prevent data loss.

Compensations and Service Credits:
- Service credits for availability breaches: credit amount = (Monthly Fee) * (downtime minutes / total minutes in month) * credit_multiplier. Credit multiplier tiers defined in Appendix 3.
- Security breach liability: subject to MSA limits; any penalties for breaches caused by Redwood negligence will follow the liability provisions in the MSA and this exhibit supplements specific obligations regarding notification and remediation.

Operational Runbooks and Handoff:
- Unexpected site conditions: runbook checklist (connectivity checks, power/UPS status, local ops contact) to be maintained in Confluence.
- Handoff: Redwood provides a 2-week hypercare window after initial deployment where on-call Redwood engineers collaborate with Customer ops via daily standups.

Variations and Optional Modules (pick list):
- Air-gapped mode: additional procedures for update packaging and manual deployment; evidence-handback contract required.
- Local-only telemetry mode: minimal outbound telemetry allowed; extra engineering effort estimate required.
- FedRAMP/IL/PCI-specific controls: available as add-ons with additional attestation and paperwork.

Open Items (placeholders for negotiation):
- [Customer to specify classification mapping and any retention exceptions]
- [Finalize appendix cipher-suite list and KMS integration model]
- [Define audit evidence format and delivery mechanism] 

Appendices (placeholders):
- Appendix 1: Approved encryption suites and algorithms
- Appendix 2: Host hardening checklist (config snippets)
- Appendix 3: SLA credit tables and measurement methodology

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- This draft intentionally balances operational flexibility (customer-managed keys, local caching) with minimal default retention to reduce legal exposure.
- Highlight items likely to generate negotiation: KMS custody, retention windows, audit scope, and liability caps.
- Suggested negotiation posture: accept KMS-in-customer-control; push for 24hr default cache retention and a 30-day post-termination purge.

Document history and versioning instructions: treat this file as a living template. For customer-specific exhibits, save as "Edge-SLA-<customer>-v1.json" and populate Schedule A and Appendices.

End of template (draft).
